newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds says pre-tax earnings could rise.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds says pre-tax earnings could rise.

text.p: Reynolds Metals Co chairman and chief executive officer, Jeremiah Sheehan, said Wednesday said that 1998 pre-tax earnings could improve by as much as $200 million or $2.00 a share, following a string of asset sales, layoffs and interest rate reductions.
Earlier, Sheehan told analysts that asset sales this year will total $900 million.

Later, speaking to reporters, Sheehan calculated that the pre-tax savings of $200 million would be made up of $40 million in corporate overhead savings, after laying off 600 people, plus a further $100 million from performance improvements, and $70-75 million in interest rate payment reductions after using the $900 million asset sales proceeds to cut debt.
